answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to hold a pearl bond: a small stake locked in escrow, slashed if the agent is caught attesting falsely. Stake alone is cheap to fake, so pair it with umber reputation, a slow-growing score earned only through verified, useful work over time, which a hollow shell account cannot buy or borrow. New identities start with zero reputation and capped earnings, so spinning up thousands of fakes costs the attacker both locked stake and months of honest work per identity, while genuine agents keep their earned standing.
